title: Security Intake Gateway and Business-Led Triage Workflow
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Enterprise incoming security and compliance asks (SOC2/ISO attestations, HIPAA posture, GDPR/DPA clauses, and open vendor questionnaires) are currently routed to three disparate queues: Support, Solutions, and Legal. This causes duplicated requests for evidence, inconsistent priority decisions, and slow time-to-resolution for high-value prospects. The existing intake playbooks are fragmented and lack a consistent decision gate that maps request intent to a deterministic SLA and response path.

Goal: Design a single 'Security Intake Gateway' that sits between customer-facing channels and subject-matter queues. The gateway should: 1) capture structured request metadata; 2) compute a transparent priority score (business impact + technical risk + contractual exposure); 3) auto-populate an evidence starter pack per request type; 4) route to Business-Led Triage lanes (Self-serve, PM/SE-led, Legal review, or Enterprise Concierge); and 5) provide automation hooks (Slack, Zendesk, API, console) with human-in-the-loop override.

Scope: PM-owned feature to build intake definitions, scoring rules, routing policies, and evidence templates. Engineering will implement the routing service and small API. Design will provide the triage UI mockups for the Console and Slack triage modal. Legal/Security will provide canonical mapping of clauses to evidence artifacts and risk flags. This ticket focuses on the product definition, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a pilot with three enterprise accounts and the Solutions team.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway captures a standardized minimal schema for intake: request_type, customer_tier, requested_artifact, SLA_requested, legal_terms_present.
Scoring engine returns a reproducible score and route for 90% of simulated questionnaire samples in the pilot dataset.
Evidence starter packs (SOC2 report stub, ISO control mapping sheet, HIPAA readiness checklist, GDPR DPIA flag list) are auto-linked into routed ticket within 10 seconds of intake.
Routing policies can be overridden by a human triage owner and the override is recorded in the audit log.
Integrations: initial connectors demonstrated for Zendesk, Slack triage modal, and a public Intake API endpoint in staging.
Pilot metrics: average ACK time < 2 business hours for high-priority items; time-to-first-evidence < 48 hours for route-to-SE lane.
proposed_flow: 1) Customer submits request through existing channels (support form, sales checklist, or vendor questionnaire upload). 2) Gateway normalizes input to canonical schema and queries the scoring engine. 3) Scoring engine applies deterministic rules (weighting for data residency, PHI scope, contractual clauses, and revenue tier) and returns a route + priority. 4) Automation applies evidence template and creates a triage ticket in the routed queue with prepopulated attachments and a suggested SLA. 5) Triage owner (business-level) reviews and either accepts the route, requests more info, or escalates to Legal. 6) All decisions, attachments, and timestamps are stored for audit and future ML training.
scoring_rubric: Weights (suggested): customer_tier 30%, PHI_or_sensitive_data 25%, contractual_liability (DPA/penalties) 20%, presence_of_external_audit_need (SOC2/ISO) 15%, time_sensitivity (RTO/RPO) 10%. Example: enterprise prospect (tier=30) + PHI flag (25) + DPA with high penalty clause (20) + SOC2 requested (15) + urgent (10) => total 100 => Route: Enterprise Concierge (SLA 24h). Lower scores route to Self-serve (automated evidence pack) or SE-assisted lane. The rubric will be stored as a JSON ruleset (managed by PM) and versioned; changes create a new routing release with rollout notes.
automation_payload_example: { "request_id": "intake-2025-03-01-914", "customer": "ACME Corp", "type": "vendor-questionnaire", "clauses_detected": ["data-transfer", "encryption-at-rest"], "evidence_requested": ["SOC2-Attestation", "Encryption-Config"], "computed_score": 78, "route": "SE-assisted", "sla_hours": 48 } (stored as a string example; real webhook uses application/json)
